----------------------------------------------------------------
EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN
“Environmental Regulations and Industrial Activity”
----------------------------------------------------------------

1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
Strategy: Difference-in-Differences (DID) augmented with an event-study.
Rationale:  
• The Clean Air Act Amendments (CAAA) of 1990 generated plausibly exogenous cross-county variation in regulatory stringency: counties classified as “non-attainment” faced much stricter emissions standards than “attainment” counties.  
• We observe plants annually before and after the policy in treated and control counties ⇒ canonical two-way panel (plant × year).  
• DID differences out common macro shocks, plant fixed effects difference out time-invariant plant heterogeneity, year fixed effects difference out nation-wide shocks.  
• An event-study of pre-policy leads tests the parallel-trends assumption and flexibly traces dynamics.

2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL
Treatment variable (T_ic):  
T_ic = 1 if plant i is located in county c that is first classified as “non-attainment” for ozone, CO, or PM under the 1990 CAAA (effective 1992 enforcement year); 0 otherwise.

Control group:  
Plants in counties never designated “non-attainment” during 1985-2000 (“always-attainment”).

Treatment timing:  
Post_t = 1 for years ≥ 1992 (first year the new standards bind). Interaction Treat_ic × Post_t is the DID term.

(If county changes status later, we treat the first effective year as the “event year” and use staggered-adoption DID/event-study; code below uses Sun & Abraham estimator.)

3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS
A1. Parallel Trends: In the absence of CAAA non-attainment, treated and control counties’ industrial outcomes would have trended similarly.  
Plausibility: Pre-1989 trends in manufacturing are similar in descriptive plots; attainment assignment thresholds were based on ambient pollution, not growth expectations.

A2. No Simultaneous Confounders: No other policy differentially hits non-attainment counties exactly in 1990–92.  
Plausibility: Other federal programs (e.g., enterprise zones) are geographically distinct; we will control for state-year policies and county-specific linear trends.

A3. Stable Composition / No Differential Attrition: The set of plants does not differentially enter/exit for reasons other than the regulation, or exit is itself an outcome we’ll study.  
Plausibility: Some exit is expected; we will show results are robust to including closed plants with zero output and to inverse-probability re-weighting.

A4. SUTVA (no spillovers): Output of an attainment-county plant is not directly affected by neighbor counties’ stricter rules.  
Plausibility: Some leakage is possible via relocation; we will explore spillovers in border-counties sensitivity checks.

4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & REMEDIES
T1. Pre-existing Differential Trends / Selection on Pollution Intensity  
• Remedy: Event-study leads; county-specific trends; propensity-score re-weighting to balance pre-treatment covariates.

T2. Plant Relocation / Sorting around Regulation  
• Remedy: Track plant IDs over time, include exit/entry as outcomes; border-pair design (compare plants within 50 km on either side of attainment border) as robustness.

T3. Concurrent Local Shocks (e.g., recessions hitting Rust Belt harder)  
• Remedy: State-year fixed effects, county-level controls for unemployment, and a triple-difference that contrasts dirty vs. clean plants within the same county.

5. R CODE OUTLINE
```r
# PACKAGES
library(data.table)    # fast data handling
library(fixest)        # DID / event-study
library(did)           # Sun & Abraham
library(ggplot2)

# 5.1 DATA LOADING
plants <- fread("census_manufactures.csv")   # one row per plant-year

# 5.2 VARIABLE CONSTRUCTION
plants[, year          := as.integer(year)]
plants[, treat         := as.integer(nonattainment == 1)]          # 1 if ever classified NA
plants[, first_treatyr := min(year[treat == 1]), by = plant_id]    # adoption year
plants[, g             := ifelse(treat == 1, first_treatyr, 0)]    # SA cohort (0 = never treated)
plants[, post          := (year >= 1992)]
plants[, did           := treat * post]

# Outcomes (log)
plants[, l_output      := log(manuf_output + 1)]    # avoid log(0)
plants[, l_employ      := log(employment    + 1)]
plants[, l_capinv      := log(capital_inv   + 1)]

# 5.3 MAIN DID (TWFE)
did_out <- feols(l_output ~ did + plant_controls | plant_id + year,
                 data = plants, cluster = ~county_id)
summary(did_out)

# 5.4 EVENT-STUDY (SUN & ABRAHAM)
# define relative year for treated units
sa <- att_gt(yname   = "l_output",
             tname   = "year",
             idname  = "plant_id",
             gname   = "g",                  # first treatment year
             xformla = ~ plant_controls,
             data    = plants,
             panel   = TRUE,
             clustervars = "county_id")
es  <- aggte(sa, type = "dynamic")
ggplot(data = data.frame(year = es$egt, att = es$att.egt,
                         se = es$se.egt),
       aes(x = year, y = att)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = att - 1.96*se, ymax = att + 1.96*se)) +
  theme_minimal() + labs(title = "Event-study: Output")

# 5.5 ROBUSTNESS: BORDER-COUNTY DESIGN
border <- plants[abs(distance_to_border) < 50]     # km
border_out <- feols(l_output ~ did | plant_id + year,
                    data = border, cluster = ~state_border_pair)
summary(border_out)
```

6. EXPECTED RESULTS
Economic theory (abatement costs raise marginal cost) predicts lower output, employment, and investment in treated counties. Prior literature finds 3-6 % declines within 5 years. I expect:  
• Log output DID coefficient ≈ –0.06 (≈ 6 % fall)  
• Employment ≈ –0.04; capital investment possibly –0.08.  
Industries with high baseline emissions (e.g., chemicals, primary metals) should experience larger effects.

7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (DID)
C1. Pre-treatment trends parallel? ………… 1  
C2. No anticipation / timing correctly coded? …… 1  
C3. No time-varying confounders correlated with treatment? … 0.5  
C4. Stable composition / minimal differential attrition? ……… 0.5  
C5. Correct inference for staggered adoption (SA estimator)? … 1  

Total ≈ 4/5 ⇒ reasonably credible with stated robustness exercises.

----------------------------------------------------------------
